title: FlowR2A: Learning Reward-to-Action Distribution for Multimodal Driving Planning
claim: Prior paradigms either select from a fixed set or sparsely supervise proposals; ours learns a dense reward-conditioned distribution over actions.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, each a mini pipeline with red dashed supervision arrows
description: A wide, short figure with three side-by-side panels, (a) Scoring-based, (b) Anchor-based and (c) FlowR2A (Ours). Each panel is a left-to-right flow with hollow block arrows. In (a), a gray box of fixed trajectory vocabulary, marked with a snowflake, feeds a blue Scorer. The Scorer is labeled p(r|a) and outputs a single selected plan. In (b), action anchors feed a yellow Action Decoder labeled p(a_gt), which produces a fan of proposals. One proposal is highlighted in thick red, and a red dashed arrow marked sparse supervision links it to GT trajectory. In (c), a target icon for reward conditions feeds a green Flow-based Action Decoder labeled p(a|r), which produces proposals. Red dashed arrows labeled simulation and flow matching link to dense trajectories. The eye goes first to the colored decoder boxes and the red supervision arrows.
caption: Comparison of multimodal planning paradigms. (a) Scoring-based methods select from a large fixed trajectory vocabulary. (b) Anchor-based methods decode multiple proposals from action anchors and sparsely supervise them with GT. (c) Our method \ourmethod{} learns the reward-conditioned action distribution $p(a|r)$ from dense trajectories, where $a$ is the action and $r$ is the reward. Red lines indicate training supervision.
abstract: Multimodal driving planning faces a long-standing tension between two paradigms: scoring-based methods benefit from dense reward supervision but are confined to a fixed action vocabulary, while anchor-based methods generate proposals dynamically yet suffer from sparse supervision constrained to a single ground-truth trajectory. In this work, we propose FlowR2A, which resolves this tension by reframing simulation-based rewards from discriminative targets into generative conditions. By learning the reward-conditioned action distribution from dense trajectory-reward pairs with a flow-matching decoder, FlowR2A unifies the dense supervision of scoring-based methods with the proposal generation of anchor-based methods in a single generative model, forcing the model to internalize the correlation between an action and its outcomes in safety, progress, comfort, and rule compliance. To balance hard safety constraints against soft progress objectives, we introduce fine-grained per-timestep reward conditioning and reward noise augmentation. The generative formulation naturally supports controllable test-time sampling via reward guidance and anchored sampling, producing high-quality proposals. FlowR2A achieves state-of-the-art results on the NAVSIM v1 and v2 benchmarks, with multimodal proposals of substantially higher quality than prior methods.
